title: alerts for SKIPPED sessions (overlap-lost, untrusted-sender, no-join-link) cannot be resolved by lkb alert-who: skipped items are never persisted locally
evidence: schedule-state.json holds only sessions that were scheduled (recordScheduled); scheduled/*.json only scheduled jobs; operations.json only webinar-release rows. runScheduleTickOnce logs result.skipped and writes nothing. So an overlap-lost / untrusted-sender / join-link alert id has no local row to match; the CLI says so on a miss.
fix_direction: The wiring unit that sends alerts should persist a small id-to-(title,start,platform) record for each alert it sends, in the same tenant state dir, mode 0600, or lkb alert-who should accept a re-run of selectAutoRecordItems over the live calendar. Out of scope here (no sender, no scheduler change).
rerated: checker 2026-10-11: medium -> high. Premise corrected: skipped overlap-lost and untrusted-sender webinar keys DO resolve via operations.json; no-join-link (cal:<id>) and needs-registration (gmail:<id>) do NOT, and needs-registration is the alert that asks the operator to act (W9 partly met).

title: alertIdFor is an unsalted SHA-256 of a session key that is low-entropy for webinar sessions: an alert holder can brute-force the meeting URL offline
evidence: Session keys are cal:<Google event id> (high entropy, about 26 base32 chars), gmail:<Mongo ObjectId> (24 hex; 4-byte timestamp + per-process random + counter, partly guessable), and webinar-<first 24 hex of sha256(identity)> where identity = https URL with only tk/token/access_token/pwd/password/utm_* removed, plus '|' and the ISO start time. The start time is printed in the alert and a Zoom meeting id is 9-11 digits, so the candidate space for a Zoom webinar is about 1e10-1e11 URLs: feasible offline (two chained SHA-256). A passcode under any other parameter name stays in the identity, which adds entropy but makes the hash a verification oracle for a guessed full URL. The recovered value is the meeting URL/id, not a stripped passcode.
fix_direction: HMAC-SHA-256 over the session key with a per-tenant secret kept in the tenant state dir (not in the alert), truncated the same way. This changes every existing alert id, so it is a contract matter for the checker and the Approver; alertIdFor was deliberately NOT changed here. lkb alert-who would then need the same secret, which it has locally.
rerated: checker 2026-10-11: medium -> high as a wiring blocker (new contract W11); not a defect of the unwired unit.

title: lkb alert-who --tenant A prints tenant B's meeting titles from the untagged state files, and its output implies tenant scoping that does not exist
evidence: schedule-state.json and scheduled/*.json live at ONE path (<repo>/raw/webinars) shared by all tenants and carry no tenant tag; --tenant only changes the tag check on operations.json. Repro (temp root, runAlertWho with real captureTenant): scheduled/b.json {sessionId:'cal:tenantB',title:'TENANT-B Board Review'} and operations.json tagged B; `alert-who <alertIdFor('cal:tenantB')> --tenant A` exits 0 and prints 'title: TENANT-B Board Review'; the only hint is the unrelated 'warning: operations.json ... belongs to a different tenant (not used)'. The miss message says 'no local meeting matches ... for tenant A'. Traversal is NOT possible (captureTenant regex rejects dot-dot-backslash-B, ../B, C: drive paths, UNC paths, A/../B, 5000 chars, NUL; CON/NUL pass the regex but the tenant is never used in a path; empty falls back to the default tenant).
fix_direction: Either state plainly on every run that uses the untagged files ('schedule-state and scheduled jobs are shared by all tenants on this machine') and drop 'for tenant X' from the miss message, or refuse when --tenant/LKB_TENANT_ID is not the default and untagged sources exist, or per-tenant state dirs. Test: a job file for B must not print under --tenant A without the notice.

title: D-015 measurement for ISS-ALERTFIX-001 is circular: 72/72 puts every formatter key straight into the candidate list; production-shaped state resolves only some skipped kinds
evidence: The test builds cand(k) for the same 6 keys it feeds the formatter, so it proves only that the hash matches. Replaying through selectAutoRecordItems(everyWebinar:true) -> reconcileWebinarSources -> projectWebinarInventory -> operations.json -> runAlertWho: overlap-lost resolved, untrusted-sender resolved, no-join-link (cal:<id>) NOT resolved, needs-registration (gmail:<id>) NOT resolved; job alerts 3/3. The row's recorded reproduction ('no tool maps an attn id back') is now trivially false because the tool exists, so it cannot show what is still missing.
fix_direction: Replace the test's candidate list with state produced by the real selection/reconcile/project functions and report resolved/total per alert kind.

title: per-job size cap is untested and a junctioned scheduled/ dir (or symlinked operations.json) is followed out of the data root
evidence: Mutation 'job size cap removed' survives (the oversize test file is whitespace, which fails JSON.parse anyway). A junction at raw/webinars/scheduled -> another dir is followed (candidate from outside printed). lstat refuses a symlinked job FILE; operations.json goes through statSync/readFileSync which follow links (symlink not creatable here, EPERM). Local-operator only; output is sanitised JSON fields.
fix_direction: Test a valid 70 KiB job file; realpath-check that stateDir/scheduled and operationsFile stay under the data root.

title: the scheduler's state files carry no tenant tag: schedule-state.json and scheduled/*.json are one shared path for every tenant on the machine
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/schedule-state.ts:247-251 recordScheduled (writeFileSync at 251) and :273-283 writeScheduledJob (writeFileSync at 283); schedule-tick.ts:17 DEFAULT_STATE_DIR = <repo>/raw/webinars; schedule-tick.ts:205 stateDir
evidence: Neither writer stores a tenant field: ScheduledEntry is {sessionKey,title,scheduledAt}, ScheduledJob is {url,until,title,sessionId}, and the directory is not per tenant. Only operations.json carries tenantId (validateOperations). Consequence for lkb alert-who: untagged sources are, by default, only counted and not searched (opt-in --include-untagged prints matches labelled 'tenant unknown (shared schedule file)'). Same consequence for any future reader of these files.
fix_direction: Belongs to the multi-tenant task: per-tenant stateDir (raw/webinars/<tenant>/) or a tenantId field in both records validated on read, plus a migration for existing untagged files. Not fixed here (scheduler write path, out of unit scope). Once done, alert-who can move those two sources into the tagged bucket and drop the opt-in flag.

title: W9 for cal:<id> / gmail:<id> skipped alerts rests on operations.json source inventory; the tick's own skipped list is only logged, so a skipped item the inventory has not seen cannot be resolved
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/schedule-tick.ts:236-239 (result.skipped is logged, never persisted); alert-who-command.ts loadCandidates (source.reconciliation.occurrences)
evidence: On production-shaped state (tick with everyWebinar:true + prepareWebinarSourceState on the same inputs) skipped no-join-link, unsafe-join-link and needs-registration resolve through operations.json source.reconciliation.occurrences (snapshot.id + source -> cal:<id> / gmail:<id>). That inventory is written by a different loader than the tick's (prepareWebinarSourceState vs loadCalendarEvents/loadCandidates), so an item present in the tick's input but absent from the inventory misses. Not verified end to end against the real poller.
fix_direction: If the wiring unit must guarantee W9, persist one small record per skipped item that can alert, in the tenant state dir: {sessionKey, startTime, source, tenantId} (never the join URL), written by runScheduleTickOnce after selectAutoRecordItems; alert-who then reads it in the tagged bucket.
